info.title: Rig API
info.description: Self-hosted deployment platform. Authenticate with the session cookie (plus `x-rig-csrf` on writes) or `Authorization: Bearer rig_...`.

post.summary: Upload a custom avatar image for your account.

delete.summary: Remove your custom avatar and reset to initials.

patch.summary: Update your own display name or avatar (built-in preset, image URL, or empty to reset).

get.summary: Active browser sessions for your account.

delete.summary: Revoke one of your browser sessions by its short id (cannot revoke the current session; use logout).

get.summary: Whether two-factor sign-in is on for you.

post.summary:
Turn two-factor sign-in off. Needs your password and a current code
(or a recovery code), rotates the current session and signs out other sessions.

Confirm the new authenticator with a code. Turns two-factor sign-in on,
rotates the current session, signs out other sessions and returns ten recovery codes, once.
Replace your recovery codes. The old ones stop working.

Start turning on two-factor sign-in. Returns a secret and its QR code;
nothing changes until it is confirmed with a code within 15 minutes.

get.summary: Alert channels in this organization.

post.summary: Add a channel. The signing secret is returned only here.

patch.summary: Rename a channel, change its events, or pause it.

post.summary: Send a test alert now and report what happened.

get.summary: Resolve an app by id, name, slug, or `project/app`.

delete.summary: Delete an app, its containers, deployments, variables and domains.

patch.summary: Change an app's settings. They take effect on the next deployment.

post.summary: Queue a deployment of the app's current source.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of deployments to return (1–200, default 50).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return only deployments created before this deployment id.

post.summary: Route a hostname to the app. Applied to the proxy at once if the app is running.

get.summary:
An app's variables. Secret values are never included; reveal them one at
a time.

put.summary:
Create or replace one variable, or atomically update a batch (`{"vars": [...]}`).
Takes effect on the next deployment.
Atomically create or replace multiple variables in one transaction.

post.summary: Read one secret's value. Every reveal is written to the audit log.

get.summary:
The running container's output as server-sent events: the last `tail` lines,
then live output when `follow=true`. Each `log` event's data is a `LogLine`.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Number of trailing lines to replay (1–10000, default 200).

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Keep streaming live lines after the initial replay (default true).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only return lines since this time (RFC 3339, Unix seconds, or relative like `10m`, `2h`, `30s`, `1d`).

parameters.name: timestamps
parameters.description: Request original container timestamps on each line.

parameters.name: grep
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter applied to each log line.

get.summary: CPU and memory use of an app's container over time.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to look. Defaults to one hour.

post.summary: Restart an app with a zero-downtime swap reusing its current image.
Start a stopped or failed app, reusing its most recent built image when available.
Stop an app's containers and take it off the proxy.

get.summary: The app's push-to-deploy webhook. Reading the secret is audited.

post.summary: Replace the webhook secret. Hooks signed with the old one stop working.

get.summary: The most recent audit log entries for the organization.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password. Sets the session cookie.
End the current session.

get.summary: The signed-in user, their organization and role.

post.summary: Change your own password. Rotates your current session and signs out your other sessions.

delete.summary: Delete a backup and its file.

get.summary: Download a backup file. It holds the database's data, so this is audited.

post.summary: Restore a backup into its database, replacing the current data.

get.summary: List databases.

post.summary: Create a database and start it. Poll the database until it is `running`.

get.summary: Engines and versions Rig can run.
Get one database.

delete.summary: Delete a database and all of its data.

get.summary: Backups of a database, newest first.

post.summary: Take a backup now. The dump runs in the background; poll the list.

get.summary: CPU and memory use of a database's container over time.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to look. Defaults to one hour.

post.summary: Reveal the password and connection URL. Recorded in the audit log.
Start a stopped or failed database on its existing data.
Stop a running database. Its data is kept.
Cancel a queued or in-progress deployment.

get.summary: A deployment's build and deploy output as server-sent events.
get.description:
Sends a `log` event per line (data is a `LogLine`), then one `end` event
carrying the final status once the deployment finishes. Reconnecting with
`Last-Event-ID` or `?after=` resumes without repeats.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Send only lines after this sequence number.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: When `after` is omitted, replay only the last `tail` lines (1–10000).

post.summary: Deploy the image of an earlier deployment again.

get.summary: The GitHub App connected to this organization, if any.

delete.summary: Forget the GitHub App. The App itself stays on GitHub until you delete it there.

post.summary:
Start creating a GitHub App. The browser posts `manifest` to `post_url`;
GitHub then redirects back to `/settings/github/callback`.
Finish creating the GitHub App with the code GitHub redirected back with.

get.summary: Repositories the GitHub App is installed on.
Branches of one repository the GitHub App is installed on, default first.

post.summary: Deploy an app from a Git host or CI webhook.

requestBody.description: Any payload. Signed with the app's webhook secret.

post.summary: Push events from the organization's GitHub App.

get.summary: Serve an uploaded organization logo or user avatar.
Everyone in this organization.

post.summary: Add a person. Returns a temporary password (valid 7 days, must be changed on first sign-in) once.

delete.summary: Remove a member. Their sessions and API tokens stop working at once.

post.summary: Give a member a new temporary password, sign them out everywhere, and revoke their API tokens.

patch.summary: Update organization name, logo URL, brand accent color, or environment badge.

post.summary: Upload a custom organization logo image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or SVG).

delete.summary: Remove the organization logo and fall back to the default mark.

get.summary: Every project in the organization, with how many apps each holds.

delete.summary:
Delete a project, its apps and their containers. Its databases are moved
to another project or deleted, as the caller chooses.

parameters.name: databases
parameters.description:
Required when the project has databases: move them to `target`, or
delete them with their data and backups.

schema.description: What happens to a project's databases when the project is deleted.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The project that receives the databases when `databases=move`.

patch.summary: Rename a project or change its description.

get.summary: Whether the instance still needs its first owner account.

post.summary: Create the first owner and organization using the one-time setup token.

get.summary: Health of the server Rig runs on: engine, proxy and resource usage.

put.summary:
Limit who may open the dashboard and API to the local network or the
tailnet. Deploy webhooks stay reachable. Refused if it would lock out the
address you are using now. On the server,
`rig-server dashboard-access public` undoes it.

Serve the dashboard on a domain of its own (with a certificate unless
`tls_mode` is `off`), or send `host: null` to serve it on the machine's
addresses over plain HTTP again. Point the name's DNS at this server
first: the old address stops serving the dashboard. On the server,
`rig-server dashboard-domain --clear` undoes it.

get.summary: CPU and memory use of the server over time.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to look. Defaults to one hour.

get.summary:
Where this machine can be reached (LAN addresses, Tailscale name) and who
may open the dashboard.
Your API tokens in this organization.

post.summary:
Create an API token for the CLI or MCP. The secret is returned once.
Requires an interactive browser session so a leaked API token cannot
self-mint persistent backdoor tokens.

delete.summary:
Revoke one of your API tokens. An API token may only revoke itself
(`rig logout --revoke`); revoking other tokens requires a browser session.

Access.description:
Who may reach a domain or the dashboard, judged by the connecting
address.

AlertChannel.description: A URL Rig posts alerts to. The URL itself is never returned, only its host.

last_error.description: Why the most recent delivery failed; empty after a success.

prefix.description: First characters of the token, for recognising it in a list.

auto_deploy.description: Git apps: deploy on every push to the branch (GitHub App webhook or polling).

cpu_millis.description: CPU limit in thousandths of a core.

health_path.description: HTTP path that must answer before traffic is switched. TCP check when unset.

host_port.description: Loopback port of the live container, for reaching the app without a domain.

oneOf.description: The latest crash the watcher saw on the live container, if any.

port.description: Port the app listens on inside its container.

volumes.description:
Paths inside the container backed by persistent volumes. Apps with
volumes deploy stop-then-start so two containers never share one.

restarts.description: Restarts of the live container so far.

AppWebhook.description: Where to send push-to-deploy webhooks for an app, and the secret that signs them.

path.description: Path on this server; prefix it with the dashboard's address.

Backup.description: A dump of one managed database, kept on the server's disk.

restorable.description: Whether this backup can be restored in place. Redis dumps cannot yet.

BulkSetEnvRequest.description: Atomically create or update multiple environment variables in one transaction.

replace.description: When true, remove existing variables that are not in `vars`.

expires_in_days.description: Days until expiry. Omit for a token that does not expire.

env.description: Environment variables set before the first deploy.

volumes.description: Absolute paths inside the container to keep across deploys.

version.description: One of the engine's offered versions. Defaults to the newest.

CreatedAlertChannel.description: A new channel, with the secret that signs its requests. Shown once.

secret.description: The full secret. Shown once and never retrievable again.

host.description:
The hostname, or null to serve the dashboard on the machine's
addresses over plain HTTP again.

Database.description: A managed database. Its password is only returned by the reveal endpoint.

host.description: Hostname apps in the same project use to reach it.

host_port.description: Loopback port on the server while running, for tunnels and admin tools.

DatabaseCredentials.description: Credentials for a database, as returned by the audited reveal endpoint.

url.description: Connection URL for apps in the same project.

DatabaseEngineInfo.description: What the dashboard offers when creating a database.

port.description:
A listener port of its own, for names that several apps share (a
machine has one Tailscale name). None serves on the standard ports.

value.description: `None` for secrets; use the reveal endpoint to read one.

challenge_token.description: Short-lived single-use challenge token returned when `code == "second_factor_required"`.

message.description: Human-readable message, safe to show in the UI.

install_url.description: Install the App on repositories here.

owner.description: The account or organization that owns the App.

GithubBranch.description: A branch of a repository the GitHub App can read.

default.description: Whether this is the repository's default branch.

GithubManifest.description: POST `manifest` as a form field to `post_url` from the browser.

manifest.description: The App manifest, as JSON text.

GithubManifestComplete.description: What GitHub sends back to the redirect URL after the App is created.

GithubManifestRequest.description: Start creating a GitHub App through GitHub's manifest flow.

organization.description: Create the App under this GitHub organization instead of your account.

GithubPushResult.description: Outcome of a GitHub App push delivery.

deployment_ids.description: Deployments queued, one per matching auto-deploy app.

skipped.description: Why nothing was deployed, when nothing was.

GithubRepo.description: A repository the GitHub App is installed on.

GithubStatus.description: The organization's GitHub App, when one is connected.

poll_interval.description: Seconds between branch polls for auto-deploy apps; 0 when polling is off.

webhook_url.description: Where GitHub sends push events for this organization.

challenge_token.description: Single-use challenge token from step 1 of two-factor sign-in.

code.description:
The authenticator code or a recovery code, when the account has a
second factor. A login without one answers 401 `second_factor_required`.

Me.description:
The signed-in principal. `csrf_token` must be echoed in `x-rig-csrf`
on every state-changing request made with the session cookie.

must_change_password.description: True when the account has a temporary password that must be changed before continuing.

MemberWithPassword.description: A member together with a temporary password, shown once.

temporary_password.description: Hand this to the person; they should change it after signing in.

cpu_percent.description:
Average CPU use. For the host, percent of all cores; for a container,
percent of one core (so it can exceed 100).

net_rx_bps.description:
Average network throughput in bytes per second. Missing until two
samples exist to measure between.

ts.description: Start of the interval, in Unix seconds.

MetricRange.description: How far back a metric series reaches.

memory_total.description: Host memory, or the container's limit. Zero when unlimited or unknown.

points.description: Oldest first. Intervals without samples are absent.

NetworkInfo.description: Where this machine can be reached, to help pick a domain.

oneOf.description:
The hostname the dashboard is served on. Without one, the proxy
serves the dashboard on plain HTTP at any address of this machine.

lan_addresses.description: Private addresses of this machine's interfaces.

your_address.description: The address this request came from, as Rig sees it.

RecoveryCodes.description: Shown once; only hashes are kept.

Role.description: Organization role. Ordered: a higher role includes every lower one.

SessionInfo.description: An active browser session for the signed-in user.

id.description: Short identifier (prefix of the hashed session token) for revoking a specific session.

token.description: One-time token printed by the server on first start.

oneOf.description: Public branding of the primary organization once setup is complete.

setup_complete.description: False until the first owner account has been created.

SourceKind.description: Where an app's image comes from.

proxy_ready.description:
False when the proxy's admin endpoint cannot be reached; apps still
run and stay reachable on their loopback ports.

TotpEnrollment.description:
A new secret to add to an authenticator app. It only takes effect once
confirmed with a code.

qr_svg.description: The URI as an SVG QR code.

TotpStatus.description: Whether the signed-in user has a second factor.

UpdateAppRequest.description:
Every field is optional; only the ones present are changed. Changes take
effect on the next deployment.

auto_deploy.description: Git apps only: deploy on every push to the branch.

health_path.description: An empty string switches back to the TCP check.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description:
Update organization branding and workspace metadata. Omitted fields are kept.
Send an empty string for `logo_url`, `env_label`, or `env_color` to clear it.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Update the signed-in user's display name or avatar. Omitted fields are kept.
Send an empty string for `avatar_url` to reset to initials.

UpdateProjectRequest.description:
Rename a project or change its description. Omitted fields are kept.
The slug stays as it was, so nothing addressing the project breaks.

UploadImageRequest.description: Upload an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or SVG) encoded as base64.

deployment_id.description: The queued deployment, when one was started.

skipped.description: Why nothing was deployed, for pings and pushes to other branches.
